column1: # Evaluation manifest -- the ground truth for `vcc_cli --eval`.
#   <wav path, relative to this file>  TAB  <what you actually said>
# Tab-separated, because a reference transcript contains spaces. '#' comments.
# Case and punctuation do not matter: both sides are tokenised before scoring.
#   1. Record. Push-to-talk, one phrase per take:
#      Say each phrase you care about a few times: normal, fast, quiet, from
#      across the room. vcc_listen prints the manifest line to paste here.
#   2. Label. Write down what you MEANT to say, not what the recogniser heard.
#      That is the whole point of a reference.
#      Read "clips worsened" first -- a filter that raises the average while
#      breaking three utterances is not ready. Then the relative gain.
#   4. Change one thing (a hotword, its boost, a rewrite rule), re-run, compare.
#      `--min-gain 20` turns it into a pass/fail gate.
# The rows below are placeholders showing the format; --eval reports missing
# files rather than failing, so it is safe to run before you have recorded
# anything. Replace them with your own takes.
# Vocabulary from the target scenarios: network/router status, device info,
# online devices, gaming sessions, guest wifi, QoS, bandwidth limit,
